utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, Judges.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. This morning we shall proceed with some questions that I'll ask you regarding the witness statement that you gave to the Prosecution. There are, in fact, two statements; one dated the 21st of February, 1996, and the other on the 19th of April, 2006. Do you remember clearly what you stated on both occasions, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I do remember.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting, Your Honour, but if the witness is going to be questioned regarding these statements, could she be provided with copies to have with her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Certainly. Let the witness be provided with the statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask my assistant to call up the statement of February 21st, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see that passage of your declaration, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you a few questions. Would you say that in Sarajevo there were other means of transport, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trams would continue running through cease-fires. The trolley buses also continued to run, those that were still roadworthy. Sometimes you could notice passenger vehicles driving down streets at considerable speed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Were there buses in Sarajevo at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, the company known as Gras, G-r-a-s, that actually owned the trams still kept them operating. But very few continued to operate, and those that did continue to operate, at great speed, because of the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, another witness testified before this Court on the 18th of January, 2007, and I will quote the witness' deposition. In the working version of the transcript, on page 14, line 7 -- lines 7 to 12, it's a very brief passage. I will read it in English. [In English] "Yes, this is parallel, and let me show you because you apparently were not in Sarajevo. This was the so-called salvation route parallel to the main road here, but it went behind the Marsal Tito barracks and in front of the railway station. And as I mentioned yesterday, at all the crossroads, there were large screens placed in order to safeguard the people against sniping." [Interpretation] Have you heard the translation, Witness, through the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, which translation were you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was reading a passage in English. Have you heard the interpretation in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard what you were saying throughout.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then I will ask you a question. Did you know anything about this "salvation route," as the witness described, the witness who appeared on the 18th of January, 2007?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us in Sarajevo had heard of that, but I'm not familiar with any details.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean -- then let me continue. Does that mean that you never took that salvation route yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The route that I took that day and the route that the trams normally took during cease-fires was not called that. It was not called the "salvation route." Those were just regular tram stops still called the same thing today, Socijalno, Pofalici, Marin Dvor, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But my question was, did you ever take a bus that - well, we will see this later on the map - that followed, more or less that road, the "salvation road," if you know it. It is a road that is parallel to the Vojvoda Putnik boulevard. It has now become Zmaja od Bosne. And that road was completely protected from any possibility of firing from either side of the confrontation lines between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the army of the Republika Srpska. Do you agree with what I have just said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't agree with you. I never rode on a bus. I like trams, as a matter of fact. My father drove a train; he was a train driver. I like trams. I still remember using them in my childhood. The street that you refer to, the Zmaja od Bosne Street, at the junction where the Elektroprivreda building was, it had burned down by this time because it had been targeted. So that's where the confrontation line was and that's where the shooting was coming from. There was a clearing there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, remember the time constraints under which we are operating. The Prosecution took about half an hour for its examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I just would like to clarify a few more points. That was one point among several.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So now if we could please call up on the screen a map that we looked at yesterday already at the end of the hearing, please. So here we see a map of Sarajevo. If we could perhaps enlarge it, please. On this map, we can see the part of the road, or the part of the itinerary, that you wanted to take on that day, the 8th of October; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is the route that the tram takes, the same direction that I was headed; to my left and then towards the right-hand side. If needed, I can point it out for your benefit. Down this blue path.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the blue line represents Miljacka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's at least what I was taught in geography classes. Blue stands for rivers; green stands for whether mountains or fields, I'm not sure. But I suppose that this should be river.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but since there are several rivers in Bosnia, is that the river Miljacka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I live right next to Miljacka. I don't see the name marked on this map, as a matter of fact; therefore, I can hardly say. Normally, if you look at maps of Bosnia and Herzegovina - and I think it's still the same today in schools - back in my time, that's one thing I know for certain, the river names were marked on maps.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but my question is: Is that indeed the river Miljacka, according to your knowledge, even if it's not written?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if it's not written, you can actually see it from the tram as you are travelling. On the way to Bascarsija or the way back, passengers on the tram are able to see the Miljacka river, although it is not quite blue, rather muddy, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you stated that the Serbs were everywhere along the right bank of the Miljacka. Do you confirm that statement today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm talking about is the area in which I lived, in which I moved about, where we had to cross obstacles, blood, pools of blood and dead bodies, on our way to get water, to get bread, on our way to visit other people, and we would be killed on the way there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, to your knowledge, all along the right bank, that was in fact the territory under the control of the army of the Republika Srpska; is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The river Miljacka runs down the right bank, if you look in that direction, that part of Sarajevo, and then the left bank, if you look at the other part of town. The course of the river was crisscrossed, and the same applied to the city's neighbourhoods, small settlements where those people lived. Some, for example, resided in Hrasno or Dolag Malta. That's where we would go to fetch water. We would run across to Grbavica, for example, on the left-hand side, and it is clear that the army of the Republika Srpska were there. That's where we had to go to fetch water, and that's where we had been shot at from.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, then, for example, do you see on the map, the right-hand side, the lower right, do you see, for example, Bistrik or Sirokaca? Do we agree that those are areas of Sarajevo on the right bank? Or, for example, you mentioned Hrasno earlier or Dolag Malta. Was that the territory under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, please? And would you take the pen and show us.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would ask that the map be marked and then tendered as evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see Hrasno, Dolag, and Malta, but I can't see the streets there, and I'm hardly able to mark them for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you so specifically. I'm just asking you to show the neighbourhood of Hrasno, please. Would you perhaps mark that with an X.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, please. We were very precise in crossing to the hill of Hrasno, Dolac, and Malta. We were very precise when we passed under a hail of bullets. I can't show that on this map simply because the streets are not there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now show us the neighbourhood of Bistrik, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues ...] where I live. I'm not familiar with that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, and also yesterday, you mentioned a neighbourhood and some buildings, and you say -- perhaps we could again call up your statement of the 19th of April. You speak of Metalka.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I think there's a problem with calling up the B/C/S version of the document, and yet it is a 65 ter document. So I think perhaps the registrar might help us to call up the B/C/S version; 2833.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The registrar is making the effort.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I don't have the B/C/S version in e-court, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have the English version. There are some technical problems, apparently, for calling up the B/C/S version, so could the interpreters perhaps help us out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's hear Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document on the screen has the name of the witness. The witness has a pseudonym, as a protective measure. Could we please go into private session while we use this, and could we please redact the last few minutes before it goes out on the live feed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let that be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, there is no need to redact anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There's no need to go into private session. Do you have a view on this, Mr. Docherty?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Only this, Your Honour. I, of course, take your word that there's no need. I'm just looking at the document on the monitor with the witness' name, but perhaps that's not going out of the courtroom or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The court deputy/usher has indicated it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we still don't see the B/C/S version on the screen, so may I just go ahead with the help of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, do that, because we are losing time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it is on page 3, paragraph 9. I would read it out and ask the interpreters to please interpret.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] "I'm sure that the tram in which you were travelling was shot at from the Metalka building in Grbavica." [Interpretation] And then there's paragraph 10, and you say the following: [In English] "... line from the place we were shot, which was the Metalka building in Grbavica, which I would say was about 200 metres away." [Interpretation] And then to come back to paragraph 9, the fourth sentence of that paragraph: [In English] "There were no military institutions, military vehicles or any other military equipment in the vicinity of the place the tram was shot at. The closest military institution to the place the tram was shot, it was the Tito barracks, which was the distance of about two tram huts." [Interpretation] So that was your statement, and my question is whether, as you said you only really knew the neighbourhood in which you lived, and in fact you didn't know precisely the military installations in Sarajevo and their vicinity. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever a cease-fire was in force, during the war and before, I always took the same tram lines, Socijalno, Pofalici and on to the Presidency, for the simple reason that I have family living on the street across the way from Skenderija. I knew those tram lines and I knew them really well ever since I was a little child.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, now you're speaking about the tram lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was regarding to the confrontation lines between the two armies that were fighting in and around Sarajevo and in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Were you aware of that conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already told you that during cease-fire and war, we took the same lines as we are taking today, and we all know all these buildings to the left and to the right to this very date. However, most of them, including Metalka, were demolished.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it will be third time lucky. I will try again. Do you know anything about the confrontation lines between the two warring factions in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to specific facilities? Can you please repeat it, in which particular location you're interested in in connection -- with what I have in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I can't discuss the locations with you because you said earlier that you didn't know Sarajevo well enough to be able to tell us anything about various neighbourhoods. So my question is: Did you know that there were confrontation lines, front lines, existing between the two armies, that is to say, the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, even small children know about that. I'm just telling you about the route on which I was wounded. If I understand you correctly, that's the only thing I can talk to you about; otherwise, please don't bother me with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And yet I heard you say, "Please don't bother me," "Don't tire me out," is what I also heard in interpretation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise if you understood it literally. I'm focused only on this particular tram route while I'm watching the slide in English, and that is what I was focused on, and your question was whether I knew about the front lines between the parties. Well, everybody knew that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's get on with the cross-examination. You're well past half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Just one last question. You have been speaking about military objectives, so did you know precisely where the military installations were located in Sarajevo; namely, in your neighbourhood that was, I think, near Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know. We didn't have time to venture out and look where these things were because most of our lives during the four years were spent in cellars.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am finished with my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And, Ms. Isailovic, you had asked all the pertinent questions you wished to ask?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I hadn't finished all my questions, but of course I want to comply with your ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How many more questions do you have that are pertinent?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I believe that all my questions are relevant, but perhaps the most relevant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll give you another five or seven minutes. One has to balance efficiency and expeditiousness with fairness. So another seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. So I would ask that a map be called up. I asked my assistant to do so. I think we already looked at this map yesterday, picture number 5 in the photo album offered by the Prosecution. I think this might take a moment. So we will see on the screen -- could we perhaps enlarge the picture a bit so that we can actually see the railroad -- the tracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I still have five minutes. So you were describing the fact that the incident occurred in the area of the tram line between the museum and the centre of town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And now, if you look at this picture, we see -- well, you spoke of an S, something like an S, perhaps the first part of an S. Do you remember approximately what the position or location of the tram was at the time of impact on the tram, please? And if you could show us on the screen using the pen and circling it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm going to mark the line as I was approaching the place of the accident. [Marks]. I was here, next to the middle door of the tram, and this is where the front door of the tram was. And that's the Socijalno stop. This is where I was standing, holding the pole, because I was on the steps.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, at the time when you were hit, is that the area where you made -- you drew a thicker line, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-35 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are not getting any interpretation. Would you please stop. We have had no interpretation in English. Would you repeat the answer so we can have it interpreted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I arrived in the tram from the Socijalno stop, marked with S. I put an arrow indicating the direction of the tram. The front section of the tram passed, which means the front door, as we call it, because each tram has three doors. I was standing at the middle door, facing the pedestrian crossing, the street, the Metalka and this part, and I was holding the pole at the steps of the tram when the shots were fired at the tram.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was my last question. Before finishing up, I would ask the registrar to mark this picture so that it may be tendered as evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be admitted as Exhibit D21, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: No re-examination, Your Honour. Before the next witness comes in, may I put briefly two things on the record. They will be short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I just wanted to -- I don't think I did this yesterday. But so that the pseudonym sheet matches the witness, I should put on the record that this is Witness 35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness 35, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving the evidence, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Your next witness, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution calls Slavica Livnjak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It has been suggested that we should have Ms. Isailovic's map tendered into evidence, as it is a better map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also have a copy of the same map that the Defence was using yesterday. I think the Prosecution map is a bit bigger and shows a bit more of the city. I should also say, though, that we got this late in the afternoon yesterday. It has not yet been loaded into e-court. It will be available in e-court tomorrow. I have one hard copy for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Could the Chamber have a copy of your map, Ms. Isailovic, until the Prosecution brings another one?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can do that. Please call the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration. Please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. I see the time for this witness is one hour for both parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, following up on the discussion that we had yesterday, Ms. Livnjak will be giving testimony pursuant to Rule 92 ter. However, I will, then, be going beyond that a little bit, and that will be the marking of aerial photographs and of maps that the Chamber, I think, has become familiar with with these various sniping witnesses. That is not in the statements that I will tender. However, I still intend to conclude the direct examination of this witness in no more than 20 to 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Madam, could you please begin by introducing yourself, by telling us your name.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Slavica Livnjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Livnjak, on the 20th of November, 1995, did you give a statement to an investigator of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And since arriving in The Hague a few days ago, have you read that statement over carefully?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In what language did you read the statement?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: In Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Was the report of your statement that you read accurate?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if today we went and asked all the same questions the investigator asked on 20th November, 1995, would we get the same answers as he got then?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd move for the admission of that statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: -- which is ter number 2849.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P94, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Later on, Ms. Livnjak, on the 24th and 25th of April, 2006, did you give another statement to a different investigator but also from this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And since arriving in The Hague a few days ago, have you taken the opportunity to read that statement over very carefully?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In what language did you read it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: In Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And when you read it over, did you find that report to be accurate?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If you were asked the same questions today that the investigator asked you back in April of last year, would we get the same answers?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I move into evidence the second statement of 24 and 25 April 2006. The 65 ter number is 2850.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be admitted as Exhibit P95, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Livnjak, over and above what is in these statements, I'm going to ask you some questions about where you were and where your tram was on the day that it was shot, which I believe was the 8th of March, 1995. First of all, is that the right date? Excuse me, the 3rd of March.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Whereabouts do you work? What do you do for a living?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: I'm a tram driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: How long have you been driving a tram in the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: It will be close to 30 years now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And how long have you lived in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: I was born in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you know the city quite well?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you to take a look at a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And unfortunately we don't have it for the monitor, so if I could ask the usher's assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you look at this map yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Is it an accurate map of the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, this is another copy of the map already in evidence as Exhibit D21.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Livnjak, is there a tram line that runs along a street, and forgive me if I mispronounce the Bosnian language, Zmaja od Bosne?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Zmaja od Bosne, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you see Zmaja od Bosne on the map that's in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And could you, with the marker, just show us -- let's get our bearings first. Could you show us, please, the Miljacka river.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And is that indicating the blue line that is sort of winding its way through the center of the map?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Above that we see a yellow straighter line. What is that yellow straighter line?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: That's the road, Zmaja od Bosne.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And is that the road along which your tram -- is there a tram route along Zmaja od Bosne?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some aerial photographs of this scene as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If I could ask the court officer to please call up aerial photo number 1, which is 65 ter number 2826.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Does this photograph show you a scene that is familiar?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: On the right-hand side of the monitor you'll find a silver pen, and if you press on the monitor, it will make a mark. Never mind. Could you take the silver pen and trace the tram line so that all of us can see it.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, please, whether on the day in March when your tram was shot, by putting an arrow on that line, what direction the tram was going? So put an arrow to show the way the tram was going.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you. As a tram driver, you noticed that the tram tracks have a curve at the place that you have just drawn; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, that is an S-curve, as we refer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And as the tram is negotiating that S-curve, what happens to the tram's speed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: The tram was fired upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm sorry if my question was unclear. My question was: When you are making that S-curve, does the -- can the tram keep going at the same speed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What does the tram have to do in order to get round that S-curve safely?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: It has to reduce speed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, the last thing I want you to mark on this aerial photograph, could you put a large X at the spot where your tram was hit in March of 1995.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, could this marked-up aerial photograph please be introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P96, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And may I ... And now may I please ask the court officer to call up aerial photograph number 3. The 65 ter number would be 2825.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: This, I believe, is already in evidence as Prosecution Exhibit P 93. Witness, is that photograph -- can you make out that photograph and the things on it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to make a couple of marks on it. First of all, just for our orient --

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I regret to say that the computer has, to use the language that was used, "crashed," and it will take a minute to restart it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I would go on, Your Honour, but the balance of my examination is all going to involve things with this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand. I also regret to say that, in my view so far, we haven't profited from the e-court system. No doubt it will improve and efficiency will be enhanced, but we'll wait for that. Judge Mindua has a question in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, while we're waiting for technology to work, I have a few questions. When exactly did the tram -- was the tram hit? Do you remember the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that it was sometime in March, March 1995. Actually, it was hit several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, was there a truce or a cease-fire in the city and the surroundings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What public or political authority had announced that there was a cease-fire so that your company actually decided to run the trams, thinking that it was safe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, an agreement had been reached between the Bosnian and the Serb politicians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One last question. Which military forces controlled the city and its surroundings at that moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The city itself was in the hands of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but once passed Miljacka - I'm talking about the river bank - that particular area was being held by the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, one last question, please. You were driving that tram, so could you estimate where the shots that actually hit your tram came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the right, the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We now have the photograph, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: To begin with, Witness, could you please mark the intersection - we saw it more clearly on the earlier photograph - where the gunfire hit your tram.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you. And then, madam, as a result of living in Sarajevo all of your life, have you become familiar with a building called the Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes. I did pass it very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Is the Metalka building on the photograph that's on the monitor in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Using the pen, would you draw an X through the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could this marked-up aerial photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the marked-up aerial photograph be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be admitted as Exhibit P96, Your Honours. Registrar's correction, Your Honours: That will be admitted as Exhibit P97.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Witness, a few minutes ago, in response to a question from Judge Mindua, you testified that you were unable to recall the exact date in March of 1995 on which your tram was shot at; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: The 3rd, the 5th. I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Would it refresh your memory if you looked at either of the statements that you gave to the ICTY investigator?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could I ask the court officer to please display the first -- actually, it would be the second page beyond the cover page of 65 ter number 2849 in the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Madam, can you read what is on the screen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes. I see it now. The 3rd of March, 1995, 12.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Case Manager, could we please have the panoramic 360-degree view of sniping incident number 14 displayed on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Madam, looking at what is on the screen, is that a fair and accurate picture, looking towards the Metalka building, of the location where your tram was shot on the 3rd of March, 1995?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And can you tell us on this picture from which direction the shots came?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: From -- I'm not sure how, I can indicate that. From between the museum and the Faculty of Philosophy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Is there a street that runs between those two buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes. There's a zebra crossing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And using that as a reference, can you tell us, did the -- did the shots come down that street?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ms. Case Manager, if we could please rotate this through 360 degrees.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: At the end of that, madam, I will ask you if this whole 360-degree view was a fair, accurate, picture of this particular spot. Would you stop there.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Stop the rotation. Do you see the building --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you see a tall building on the screen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And in your statements you talk about pulling into the shelter of a building in order to get the wounded off your tram. Is the building you stopped behind on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Which building is it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: The tall one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If we could continue the rotation to the end, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Madam, I have three last questions and then I'll be done. On the day that your tram was shot, can you tell us what the visibility was like? And by that I mean, was there fog, leaves on trees, anything that made it hard to see more than a few hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Visibility was good. It was a bright, sunny day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Were there any Bosnian army troops or other military facilities of the Bosnian army close by to the tram when it was shot?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Was there any military combat going on near the tram at the time it was shot?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. My name is Branislava Isailovic, I'm an attorney with the Paris bar, and I represent General Dragomir Milosevic, the accused in these proceedings. I'm going to ask a few questions, as is usually done here, and it's going to have to do with what you stated both in your written statements to the Prosecution, which are introduced as evidence here. You said that you remember everything you stated on November 20th, 1995, and on April 23 and 24, 1996. Do you still confirm that? Do you still maintain that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please call up the map that the Prosecution used earlier, map -- the 65 ter number 2826. If we're lucky, the gods of technology will be with us and the map will be displayed extremely soon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So before looking at the display, earlier when asked by the Prosecution, you said that all this occurred during a curve. The impact occurred while you were taking that curve at that place that's -- well, now we have the map on the screen, at the place you were shown earlier. Do you confirm that? Could you please answer?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes. As I was entering the curve.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us today whether your tram was in two parts, two parts connected by some kind of -- I can't find the exact word. This is really technical. It's some kind of articulation, hinge. So was it a tram with two cars connected together?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, a so-called accordion. That's the term that we use.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Accordion, that's the technical word I was looking for. So the two cars of the tram were connected by this device?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: As the tram driver, you were in front; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is the first car longer than the second car, or are both cars -- or is it the other way around?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: The first is slightly longer than the second.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And the doors -- there are two doors in the front car and there is a third door in the second car, after that accordion; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where the -- how many doors there are to that tram, at least in the first car, before the so-called accordion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: The first car has two and the second also has two.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecutor asked you a question earlier. He asked you what happens when you start entering into the curve, what happens to the speed of the tram. I'm sure you remember this question that was put to you.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Can you please repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, no problem. Earlier the Prosecution asked you a question about the tram. He asked, What happens to the tram when you're going to the curve? What happens to the speed of the tram? I can tell you what your answer was. You said that you slow down in order to be able to negotiate the curve. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So this is the question that I would like to ask you: You've been driving the tram for 30 years. So physically, what happens to the position of that accordion and to the second car when you're negotiating to take the bend? I'd like to know whether the tram really stays in a straight line or whether it changes, its shape actually changes, because you're negotiating the curve, or you're going to negotiate the curve.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Well, gradually, as you enter the bend, it begins to bend.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when you're in the curve, because on the photograph we see that there are two actual curves -- you see that on the screen; right? It's an S, so you go right and then you go left; is that it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At that very moment, can you tell us what the tram looks like? Could you describe it, whether its shape actually changes. Would it look like any kind of object that would be familiar?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Well, as it enters this bend, it sort of bends and it looks like the moon, you know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: The moon? You mean yesterday's moon, like it was yesterday, last night?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Because it can be a full moon and then it's a circle, or it can be a crescent.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Full moon.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: No, that can't be. What exactly -- what shape are you talking about? I'm sure there was a little problem with translation. You said "mladi mesec"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But "mladi mesec" is not full moon, it's crescent. There was a translation error. So it's not like a full moon, like a circle. It's not that kind of moon that you were talking about. "Mladi mesec" is not when the moon is full, when it's a circle.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's clear now. Is it fair to say that when the train has this crescent shape, both cars are exposed but in different areas? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, but it really depends on its position.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. But can we agree to say that when the tram actually adopts this crescent shape, the two cars are -- the two cars face different sides, and they're facing two different sides.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, but that's once it's reached the --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: That's in the curve. That's what we -- right into the bend. Now, the day your tram was hit, there was a criminal investigation. Were you involved in that? Do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, there were --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, here again I have a document that has not been introduced by Prosecution as evidence, even though I obtained it from the opposite party. This is document 739 in the 65 ter list. It's a -- it's the criminal investigation report. I guess that there is an English translation; unfortunately, we did not get it. However, I wanted to use this report regarding the on-site inspection after the incident, and I would like -- I would like to be granted leave to use this report. It's 65 ter number 739. If I could just get confirmation from the witness. On screen we have this report, and if you have no objection, can I please use it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We may be handicapped by the lack of translation. Does Mr. Docherty have this document translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in Bosnian, this is a several-page document. I've just been looking and I found -- I have found one page. That doesn't mean I don't have the others, just that I'm still looking. We can proceed with the interpretation. It will be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's time for the break. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: We were on this report, and one of its pages is displayed on the screen. Witness, you told us earlier that you remember this criminal investigation that was conducted after the incident.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: The policemen went on site. They made a statement, and in the text, in the dense part of this text, this is what we can read. We can read that tram number 268, arriving towards Bascarsija, was hit in the second car, between what we call this accordion and the third door from the front, from the driver's seat. Can you see that on the screen?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you note the same thing yourself?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier you said that there are two doors in the second car, after the accordion, and you said that this car is shorter than the first car. Could you tell us where that third door is located, the first door after the accordion? What is the distance between the accordion and that third door?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Well, approximately, they're about 1 or 2 metres from the accordion; the accordion and then the door after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Would it be 1 metre or 2 metres? Is it closer to 1 metre or closer to 2 metres?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Well, I didn't build the tram so I can't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember the victims that were in the tram? Do you remember where they were sitting? Were they in the first car or in the second car?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: In the second car.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could my case manager please display part of the map that we saw earlier and that we presented yesterday. I'm calling it our map. But on this map you see the part of town where you have the place the tram was hit. Of course we need some time for the map to be displayed. It is displayed now. Could it please be rotated in the right direction and zoomed in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, Witness, you talked about other dangerous areas. Do you remember that? So is it fair to say that you stated that the Holiday Inn, which is the place where the incident actually occurred, there's also Pofalici and Bristol.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please show us on the map these two locations, Pofalici first, please, where the tram ride was dangerous. That's where the tram road -- where it was dangerous. That's Pofalici. Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: It's this junction, so it's right before where the red line stops. It's right before the place where the incident of March the 3rd actually occurred; am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: This is Elektroprivreda. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a dangerous place. Could you please mark this with a P, like Pofalici, as being a dangerous area.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And you're also talking about Bristol. Can we see that location on the map?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No. This map is a small one. I can't. I can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I no longer have any map. I have a bigger map. Could we please have it on the ELMO, maybe, in order to see exactly what location we're talking about. It would be interesting to see where the Bristol is actually located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you could please move it around slightly. Thank you. I think it's focused.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So could you tell us exactly where Bristol is on this map.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But we also saw this on the other map. Maybe it's best to have the markings on a single map. You're absolutely sure it's in that location, in that area, close to Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes. A little bit further from Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that's the case, since that location can be seen on the map we used earlier, could we please display the map that we saw earlier, the one that was annotated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're now moving from map to map.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's number D. I'm told I have to give the number of this map. It's D00-02-61.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So on this map, could you please locate Bristol. Is that the same place that you already marked?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So this is another dangerous location, at least for trams. Could you please tell us what's there? We see Pofalici. That's at the foot of Humsko Brdo. Do you know Humsko Brdo? It's a hill.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes. Pofalici is there, but it's pretty far from Hum. I mean the tram tracks are pretty far.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And on the other side, on the right bank of the Miljacka, is Hrasno, which is a lot closer to that location. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, but Grbavica is close as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But the Hrasno neighbourhood, are there any highrises in Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Hrasno? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that Hrasno was on a territory controlled by the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that the confrontation line was between Hrasno and Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that because I didn't take part in any of that in order to be able to have this knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement you say that throughout the war you lived in Sulejman Filipovic Street. Is that true? And you said it was very dangerous there.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Why was it so dangerous?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Because of the attacks, the shelling, the shooting, the sniping.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that your street -- I looked at the map, but your street is in Dobrinja; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that Dobrinja is in Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: No? Then will you please have the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But first I'd like to introduce the other map into evidence. We'll do that later anyway because we already have the map on the ELMO. Can we move it to the right slightly so we can see the Dobrinja. It's the eastern part -- no, it's the south-east -- no, the other side, please, south-west. And move it up slightly, if possible. A bit more. No, the other way around. The other way around, please. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on this map now, do you see your neighbourhood, Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me, could you make the witness indicate the place on the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, could you show Dobrinja on the map, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this neighbourhood of Dobrinja was split between the units of the BiH and the units of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please show us your street, where you lived. And approximately, so we know exactly what part of the neighbourhood you lived in. I'm just asking for a rough estimate. You're closer to Nedzarici or closer to Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: It's closer to Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sure you know that right above was a hill or a mountain called Mojmilo. Do you know it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please show us where it is, to see where it was located in reference to your own neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that that hill or mountain was totally controlled by the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: I am not meddling with these kinds of things, nor do I know anything about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An objection with the transcript. The witness said "I'm not interested in military business," and on the transcript this is not written.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So did you say that you were not interested in any -- in military business?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: I know nothing about these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But in your statement you said that your tram was hit from the aggressor's line. Is it true that you said that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So since you're not interested at all in military affairs, how did you know where the aggressor was and who the aggressor was?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Well, I knew as far as this line, this part, was concerned, because we had protection from UNPROFOR in order to enable us to do our work.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But according to you, who was the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And agressing whom, and agressing which territory?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: The aggression conducted by them against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are you thinking about the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina that was in conflict with the army of Republika Srpska? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you had been driving a tram for 20 -- 30 years; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So you're very familiar with the organisation and the running of your company.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether there were other means of transportation in Sarajevo at the time?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard about the buses that were using the so-called "salvation route"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, there were buses, but they were taking people to work, people who were under work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, did you know that those buses were driving along this so-called "salvation route"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, did you know what route those buses were driving along? Were they driving along the same routes as the trams?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you right, they did not drive along the same routes as the tram; right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not too sure about your answer, about the meaning of your answer, so let me make this clear. These buses did not ride along the same routes as the trams; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes, that's true, they didn't take the same routes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know where -- did you know what routes those buses were actually taking?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that these buses were not owned by your own transportation company?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: They belonged to our company but they took workers to work, to hospitals, and all those who were under work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And as a citizen, as a worker in that company, have you ever heard that these buses would have been hit, that there would have been victims aboard those buses?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes. It happened at Mojmilo to one of the buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And have you heard about something that would have happened to those buses in the junction we mentioned as being extremely dangerous, between Hrasno and the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Well, Hrasno is not in front of Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: No, but earlier, on the map you showed us that in Hrasno, next to Bristol, there was a place that was really dangerous for the tram ride.

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And then after that there was a whole part of the road between that point and the Holiday Inn, and my question deals with that junction, Hrasno, which is a dangerous point, and the other dangerous point which was located at the Holiday Inn. Have you ever heard about incidents that would have occurred regarding buses in that junction?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Then you just told us that you were not interested in military affairs, but in your statement you say that there were no military targets or objectives around the Holiday Inn where the tram was hit. But are you aware of any military objectives that would have existed?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it because you were not interested in military affairs or is it because there were no such targets?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: There were no such facilities because UNPROFOR was there to protect us and to guarantee that nothing would happen.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please answer to my last question. According to you, what exactly is a military target?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Docherty, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Just on one point, Your Honour, if I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Madam, Ms. Isailovic was just asking you about military targets. On the day your tram was shot and at the place your tram was shot, did you see with your eyes any uniformed soldiers other than UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Tanks?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mortars or artillery pieces?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Other than UNPROFOR, did you see anything of a military nature at the place your tram was shot on the day your tram was shot?

utterances.speaker: SLAVICA LIVNJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but I forgot to ask for this annotated map to get a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let it be given a number. Before we do that, Judge Harhoff has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Madam Witness, I would like you to indicate on the map on the ELMO with the silver pen where your tram was hit that day, on the 3rd of March, 1995. If you can. Madam Witness, if you can't find it on this map - because I do admit it is quite small - then perhaps could you show it on the map on the ELMO, the other map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So that's the spot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, what's the map that you wish to have admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the map that we have on the screen, DD00/0261, with the annotations made by the witness, the dangerous places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And regarding the criminal investigation, which is a 65 ter document, number 739, I would also like -- well, maybe I can first offer it for translation, and get a provisional marking. We only have a B/C/S version. I'm told that an English version also exists, so could I please get a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Please ensure that we have the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the map marked by the witness will become Exhibit D22, and the document 65 ter number 00739 will become Exhibit D23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Madam Witness, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving it. And you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next up, Ms. Marcus, I believe?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The Prosecution calls Witness 62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit, and you may begin, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President and Your Honours. May I request the court officer to show the witness a pseudonym sheet, as this witness is protected.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you please confirm for us that your name is as it appears on that sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. May I request that it be shown to the Defence and to Your Honours. May I request that this pseudonym sheet be entered into evidence under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P98, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Good day to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you kindly tell the Court your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: All my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What is your training and education in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I went to secondary school for traffic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I work for an Italian company.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, how old were you when the war began?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Fourteen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Where were you living between August 1994 and November 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: In which part of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can he just tell us what work he does for the Italian company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I work with espresso coffee. I'm a distributor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What town were you living in at that time, between August 1994 and November 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Novi Grad.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Between those dates - again, August 1994 and November 1995 - with whom were you living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: With my mother and sister.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How did you get access to food?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It was difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: There was a war on. Sarajevo was surrounded. It was difficult to get any food aside from the humanitarian aid that kept arriving.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And who was responsible for feeding your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How did you get water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: That was difficult, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you go out of your house to get food and water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And how was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Water came in special water tankers and food came in shipments of humanitarian aid which would then be distributed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was it easy to go out and get food and water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Why was that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Shellings were quite frequent and sniping, too. It wasn't really that easy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Between August 1994 and November 1995, what did you and the other civilians do to avoid snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Mostly we ran.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm now going to ask the witness questions relating to scheduled sniping incident number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, how did the morning of the 24th of October, 1994, begin for you, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It was dreadful.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Let's start at the beginning. What was the first thing that happened that morning, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: My best friend was killed that morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Can you take us to the beginning of the morning and tell us, step by step, what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It was his birthday, as a matter of fact. We were supposed to celebrate his birthday, but he was off with his mother to see some relatives. I was supposed to go. So we agreed that we would celebrate his birthday the night before, on the evening of the 23rd. We were in his flat; we were having fun, listening to the radio. We were off to bed. And the next morning, at about 6 in the morning, we were outside the building and we went to a department store that was part of our building. It was called Vemeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I just want to interrupt you. Slow down a bit please, for us. We'll take it step by step. Let's go over what you've just told us. First of all, can you please tell the Court the first name of your friend you're referring to, whose birthday you celebrated the night before the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Adnan. His name was Adnan.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. And you said you were celebrating through the night, and at 6.00 in the morning you went out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. And when you left your house at 6.00 a.m., where did you go, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: As I pointed out, there was a small department store that was part of our building. It was called Vemeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And how far, approximately, from your house was the Vemeks store?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: In normal circumstances, the distance ran into about 40 metres, but this was wartime and we had special passages we used behind the building, so it would have taken us about 5 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How long did you stay out, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Between 10 and 15 minutes at the most. Not long.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And why was your destination the Vemeks department store?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Our whole building, all the people who lived there, would use that place to get out. It was considered a safe passage out of the building, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So after you stayed out for about 10 or 15 minutes, then where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: We went back to my flat.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And then how long did you remain in your flat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: We remained for a while. I think we even had breakfast. And then we were off again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Where did you head out to this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Again through Vemeks, and then on to the flat.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. When you left the house -- your apartment the second time, you were heading towards Vemeks. Did you actually go to the Vemeks department store?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.
