utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And did you stop to speak to anybody on your way there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: When we came to Vemeks, we saw a friend of ours, a girl who was born on that same day, and we approached her to congratulate her.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At this point when you were speaking with your friend, how many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Four of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who those four were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Adnan, this girl called Natasa, Ermin and myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Who was Ermin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Ermin was a mutual friend.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How long did the four of you stand talking with Natasa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: About two or three minutes, the time it takes to say, "Happy Birthday."

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Ermin, Adnan and I were off to Vemeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you possibly describe for the Court, please, the Vemeks department store. What's on its left, what's on its right, how does it appear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Looking at the department store, to the left there was the main street and to the right there was the entrance, just outside of the building, some sort of a passage, that was actually part of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So the three of you were walking away from Natasa's house and towards the Vemeks department store; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And in what sequence were you walking, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Ermin walked ahead of us and then Adnan and then I.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How far did you get, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: As far as the passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Ermin came to the wall. He stepped over the wall. There's a low wall that you need to step over. So Adnan was just about to do that and at this moment I heard a shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How far were you, approximately, from the passageway when you heard the shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: About 10 metres, up to 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did you do when you heard the shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: We started to panic and run, Ermin and I. We didn't know what was going on. All I heard at the time was a scream, someone calling my name. I turned around and I saw Adnan standing there, his face pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I turned around to face him. I grabbed hold of him, not knowing at the time what had happened. I pulled him closer to me and started pulling him towards Vemeks. I realised at this point in time that Adnan had been hit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I saw a friend of mine, called Fahrudin. I called him over to give us a hand, since I realised that Adnan had been hit. Fahrudin came with a bandage. We took off the top of the tracksuit that Adnan was wearing, and we realised there was a bullet hole on his shirt.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, to clarify, did you hear one shot or two shots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I heard one when Adnan was hit; however, when I started pulling Adnan towards Vemeks, I heard another shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So you were with your friend Fahrudin and you took off Adnan's jacket; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what did you notice about Adnan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: We realised there was a hole in his chest, the right half of his chest. We realised he had been hit. We took off his shirt. He was naked down to the waist at this point. Fahrudin turned his body around, and we realised that there was an exit wound on the left-hand side of his lungs.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you please indicate for the Court, on yourself, where the entry wound was on Adnan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Right here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And where the exit wound was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: The other side of the shoulder blade.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could the record indicate that the witness has shown the entry wound on the front right shoulder and the exit wound on the back left shoulder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did Adnan make any sound?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No. He tried to draw breath but it came out more as a gurgle. He wasn't really able to breathe.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And how did he look?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: He was in a dreadful state. He was white, pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did you do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: We placed this bandage on him. In the meantime a vehicle had arrived from somewhere, some sort of a makeshift vehicle, to take him away. Other people gathered. We placed Adnan in a car and then they were off to the Dobrinja hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you describe this vehicle for us? Was this an ambulance or a private vehicle? What kind of vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No, it was not an ambulance. It was a civilian vehicle, some sort of a delivery vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you have access to emergency vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you explain why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: There was a lot of sniping around my area. It simply wasn't possible for them to even go there when called. There was the hospital at Dobrinja, which was sort of close, so that's where one took people, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you go with Adnan in the ambulance, in the private vehicle that you were using as an ambulance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No. It was Fahrudin who went.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Where was Ermin during this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Frankly, I don't know. I was in a state of shock. I didn't see a thing. I didn't see him leave, or where he left.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When the vehicle left with Adnan, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I stayed at Vemeks.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, did Adnan survive this sniping incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When did you find out that Adnan had died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: About half an hour later, when Fahrudin returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What did Fahrudin tell you, exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: He said that Adnan died on the way to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How old was Adnan on that day, the 24th of October, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Fourteen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That was his birthday, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, was there any military-related facility of any kind in the area where that incident took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Some way off from the place where the incident occurred there was a dormitory, some 50 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And can you describe the dormitory? Was it an official military facility, or what precisely was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No. This was not an official military installation. It was more like a privately-owned flat where the military stayed during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did the soldiers use the passageway next to Vemeks to go in and out of that small dormitory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were there -- was there any military activity in that area of any kind on the 24th of October, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you see any ABiH soldiers at all at that location on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you please describe for the Court how you were dressed on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I was dressed in a tracksuit, which means sports clothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What was Ermin wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Ermin had blue jeans on and a T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what was Adnan wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Also a tracksuit like me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What was the weather like on that date, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It was a pretty nice day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Before the 24th of October, 1994, was that passageway next to Vemeks known to be a very dangerous location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What about after Adnan was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you and the other residents of that block do anything to protect yourselves from being shot at that passageway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes. We put a blanket. We put it -- a kind of hanging blanket.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And did the blanket assist you in protecting yourselves from being shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: For a couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Since there was a lot of shooting, the blanket was torn in ribbons, just -- there were just remains of it there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, just to go back one moment to the clothing you were wearing on that day. Can you tell us, if you recall, the colour of the tracksuit that you were wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I think it was blue.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Do you recall the colour of Ermin's clothing on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I think that Ermin's T-shirt was black.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what about Adnan's clothing? The colour, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Greyish black or grey with some black pattern.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness, did you meet with Prosecution investigators in the summer of 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And on that date, did you indicate on camera where the shot which killed Adnan came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, as this witness is protected, may I request we move into private session simply for the showing of the video where he himself appears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you confirm today the information that you provided to the ICTY investigator, as we have seen in this video clip?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you provide that information to the investigator of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court anything about any differences between how this area looked on the day of the incident and how it looked on this video.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes. There's one difference. The trees have grown and are full of leaves.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The blanket that you mentioned earlier, was that blanket put up to block the passageway before Adnan was shot or after Adnan's incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It was put up afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At the end of the video clip we just watched, a building was zoomed in on. Can you identify for the Court what that building was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: That's the centre for blind children and children with impaired vision.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what was the area of town called where the school for the blind was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, who was in control of the area known as Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was there anything obstructing the view from Nedzarici, where you say the shots came from, to where your friend was standing, where you and your friend were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd now like to ask the court officer, please, to pull up a photograph of the location where Adnan was killed. It's 65 ter number 2862.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't have that image in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: May I have one moment, please, to confer with the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm informed by the case manager that it is there and that she's released it. No? You don't have it? Mr. President, Your Honours, the reason that we wanted to have the one that was submitted in e-court is so that the witness could actually mark some locations on it. We do have the same photograph as part of the DVD, with the 360-photograph, so we could show him that one but it will -- he won't be able to mark it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's do that, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. So I request the case manager to please pull that up.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you see an aerial view of the location of that incident on the 24th of October, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what is identified by the three red circles that we see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: This passage is marked with these circles.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us which side of the passageway is marked with those circles? Is it the side from which the shots came from or the side where you and Adnan were standing when Adnan was shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: That's where the bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like you --

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Sorry, Court Officer, is it possible for the witness to use any kind of implement to indicate -- no, it's not. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could you describe on the picture where the school of the blind is, if possible, with words.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: There are two larger buildings down there and two smaller ones in between them. One has a dark red roof; the other one is grey, in the bottom left corner. So this is the centre for the blind.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you say that this photograph is a true and accurate representation of the origin of fire and the place of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: May I now request the case manager to show the DVD, which has the 360-degree photograph of the location. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I'm going to ask the case manager to rotate the photograph slowly to the right, and as she does that, would you please stop us when you see the Vemeks department store.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Case Manager, I'd request you to pause, please, when the witness reaches that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay, please start.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: You can stop now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is this the Vemeks department store?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now I'll request the case manager to continue, and please pause us when we reach the passageway from which the shots came.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: You can stop here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: If we can please just continue the rotation to complete the 360 degrees. Thank you. Mr. Witness, would you say that this photograph is a true and accurate representation of the location where Adnan was shot on the 24th of October, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: How, if at all, does this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence finds it difficult to understand -- well, I completely agree with these -- I'm impressed by these technical miracles that allow us to have a 360-degree view, but would it be possible to locate specifically the point around which we are rotating? What is the central point? During my cross-examination, I might be able to come to that, but perhaps it would be more practical to know exactly what is the central point, because we saw earlier a recording or a video from an aerial view. But frankly, I can't really locate exactly where we are, whether it's on one side or the other of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you able to identify the central point, Ms. Marcus?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when you say "central point," are you referring to the actual spot of the shooting or are you referring -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you mean, that if it's a circle, it must have a center?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I imagine that this recording is helping us to imagine that we are on site. It's as if we were on site and we were turning around to see everything that is around us. But we need to know where we are. Where are we standing? What is the point -- well, let's say if I were there, I would be standing to have this 360-degree view, to see all that we can see on the screen - I hope this is clear enough - to know exactly where I would be standing in relation to which we see something. Perhaps if we could look at the map of Nedzarici, one could show us that this is where you're standing and this is all you can see as you look around, around this axis. So it's the viewpoint of the person of -- where is the person standing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The person taking the photograph, are we able to identify that point?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, I've understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, when you saw that 360-degree photograph, can you please identify for the Court from what spot was that photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: As far as I can see, the person who shot this photograph was standing two to two and a half metres from the spot where Adnan was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And is that two to two and a half metres away from the passageway or two to two and a half metres closer to the passageway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Towards the wall.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Does that answer the learned counsel's request?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, if she has other points, she can raise them in her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. May I request that this portion of the DVD with this 360-degree photograph be entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P99, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, just a few last questions. Could you tell the Court a little bit about your friendship with Adnan.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: We were very close. We were like brothers. We slept in each other's flats. His mother was like my mother, and vice versa. That was something -- we grew up together.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you attend Adnan's funeral?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Court how Adnan's death has affected your life.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It was horrible. Horrible.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness W-62, you clearly went through an extremely painful experience, and of course the Trial Chamber feels a great deal of compassion, but our concern is to establish the truth, the truth of the facts, the incident, and also to determine liability, to identify the author or authors in order to establish their responsibility or liability. That is why I would like to ask you a few questions. You spoke of a military dormitory or soldiers in the vicinity. Unfortunately, we don't see the picture anymore on the screen. Perhaps we might come back to it. Perhaps it would be good to see exactly where the dormitory was, where soldiers slept in the vicinity. Well, nevermind, since there's no image anymore on the screen. I'll come to my second question, which is more important in my mind. You said that the shots were coming from the passage or the building located at the end of the passageway, and that in that building there was the centre for blind children. And this was in a place under the control of the Republika Srpska forces. How can you know that the shots were coming from there? Did you have any means, I don't know, any practical means? I know you're not an expert in this field. But how do you know that the shots came from that direction? And my further question would be: Across from this school for blind children, were there not other buildings from which the shots could have originated? And in that case, if there were such buildings, by whom were they controlled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, here's how it was: If you were to pass by this passageway, you can see the school for the blind children through the passage, where holes were made in order to shoot through them. So everyone living in the neighbourhood could see that. So the second question was about the buildings between the passageway and the place of incident. There were garages there, but they were not high enough to obstruct the view. And I think there was a question about who controlled the area. It was under the control of the army of BH. I'm talking about these garages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The garage below the centre for blind children; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. They were between the passageway. If we can have the photograph back again, you can see sort of two grey squares.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have actually a hard copy of the photograph. Will that help, to be pointed to on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the garages that I mentioned, one is here and the other one is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I just ask you, where were the holes made in this school? At what level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately I cannot show it to you. They were at the front of the building, closer to the top of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the building would have had how many floors; do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe there were three floors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And these holes were at the top, the top-most floor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between the floor and the roof, at the very top of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We have to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please begin, Ms. Isailovic. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, Your Honours. I'm told now that the photograph that was not markable before has now been loaded in and can be marked by the witness. With your permission, I'd just ask him to mark three spots on the photograph and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: May I request the court officer to please pull that up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you please mark, with that pen that you've been given, on this photograph the location of the garages that you were referring to earlier. And could you mark it with a G for garage, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you also please mark for the Court the area of town that you referred to as Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And lastly, could you please mark for the Court the building that you referred to as the school for the blind. You could mark it with an S for "slijepi," S for blind in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I put an additional question to the witness, just an extension of the video that was offered by the Prosecution, because I have -- I do not have a full understanding of what we saw on the video. Now, if you suggest, Mr. Witness, that the shots came from the school of the blind, then my question would be that, on the video it looked as if the bullets went through the passageway and hit someone who was on the other side of the building. So that means that if the shots came from the location S shown on the picture on the e-court, towards the direction where the three red spots are, then my question is: Is that the entrance of the tunnel shown by the three red spots, and so that the incident occurred on the other side of the building? Is that what can be deferred from this picture? Do you understand my question, Mr. Witness? I'm sorry, it was perhaps a bit awkwardly put to you, but I hope you're getting the gist of what I'm asking for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand the question. This is the entrance of the passageway, and the incident occurred at the other end, at the other end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: At the other side of the building that can be seen here, the tall white building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that's right. Past the passageway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Just for clarification, Mr. Witness. I'm sorry. If the three red circles on the picture shown in the middle of -- a bit above the middle of the picture, if that marks the entrance of the passageway, then your suggestion is that the shots were fired from the school of the blind upwards towards the entrance of the passageway, through the passageway, and then hit Adnan on the other side of the passageway, which we cannot see here because it's on the other side of the building. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm sorry. May I move to admit this marked photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let it be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P100, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. I'm Branislava Isailovic, a member of the bar in Paris, and I represent the Defence of Dragomir Milosevic, the accused in this case. I'm going to ask you a few questions concerning your witness statements, the statements you made for the Prosecution and also today before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to start out with the same picture, the picture used by the trial attorney, but could we see this same picture without any annotations, a virgin copy. It has been explained to me that -- it is number, I think -- the same picture, the picture we already see on the screen, but might it -- perhaps my learned colleagues could help me with the 65 ter number. I don't have it on hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I believe the 65 ter number is 2862.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, here we have the same picture as we did earlier, and what I'm interested in -- in fact, earlier I also was interested in the exact location of the garage or garages, but what I'm particularly interested in is whether you know what these objects are, these objects or facilities between what you showed us as the school for the blind and the alleged point of impact, the entrance of the passageway. There is what seems to be some construction, some facilities. Could you tell us exactly what it is, what these are, and to annotate the picture as you did earlier; for example, the building that is nearest to the centre for the blind, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: There's one thing I would like to say first. This photograph was taken perhaps a year ago. Some of the buildings were added. When the incident occurred, most of these buildings were not there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So then my question is the following: Which of the objects that you see on the -- well, between the centre for the blind and the entrance to the passageway, which of those buildings already were on site at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Should I mark these for you?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, could you tell me, the first building nearest to the centre for the blind, could you tell us exactly what that building was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: The square or the market.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is that a high building, rather high, or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: No. A low one. Those were boxes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And the second building as you come closer to the passageway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: You mean the X in the middle?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: That's a garage.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Are those garages of the same type as those that are closer to your building, in other words, closer to the alleyway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask that this picture be marked, the picture that has been annotated by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be admitted as Exhibit D24.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has been explained to me that I should proceed as follows: If I would like to explore a video sequence or the 360-degree pictures tendered by the Prosecution, I must ask for their assistance in order to have it called up on the screen. So I would ask you, please, to call up the video sequence, and afterwards, I would like to discuss it with the witness. That isn't the video clip. It should be number 65 ter 27117 showing the investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: May I just request, then, that we move into private session to protect the identity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, since you lived in the neighbourhood - perhaps you even had friends who lived there - above the alleyway there was an apartment that was about what size, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps there's a slight misunderstanding due to interpretation. I asked you if there was an apartment, but approximately what size, what surface area? Was it the size of one apartment? Were there two apartments? Is it a big apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: The answer is yes, it was as big as a flat, which means the passageway's as long as the building is wide. The building has flats on both sides, if you see what I'm trying to say. The area was in terms of square metres. The passageway or the flat above it is really not something that I can specify.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Just a detail, because you just said on both sides, so do I understand you correctly that there were "urezi", as we call them, on both sides, there were entrances on both sides?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I'm sorry, entrance? What sort of entrance? To what, exactly?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I was thinking of what we call "haustor".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It only has one entrance on one of the sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, they were only on the side -- on the side where you were during the incident, there is an entrance or entrances to the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And in the video you stopped for a moment, or you held the position in which your unfortunate friend was when he was mortally hit by the shot. Is it true that his right shoulder was turned towards the alleyway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And the alleyway was, therefore, on your right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: When the trial attorney asked you questions earlier about the wounds, the exit and the entry points of the bullet, I think you said that the bullet entered on the right-hand side, entered straight but not on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: The wound was on the right side, the entry wound, on the right. Nearly the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This may seem to be an unfortunate question, but, well, we have to -- well, the issue here is the guilt of a person so I have to insist. But did the bullet enter from the front or from the side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: These questions are causing quite a bit of stress; that's true. The bullet entered from the front right side, from the front, on the right, if you look at the direction we were headed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I would like to ask you a few questions regarding the content of your testimony today and your witness statements of November 15th, 1995, and May 22nd, 2006. First of all, you say that at the time you were 16 years old, not older than that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So I suppose that at that age you were considered to be a young boy, an adolescent rather than an adult.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Frankly, I'm at a loss as to what to answer. I was the man in the house, as they say where I come from. I had my mother and my sister to look after. It was a commitment that I had as a male, the only male in the house. Frankly, I didn't really like it very much when others viewed me as a small boy, a child.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand quite well. That was the feeling that you had, the way you saw yourself, and that's quite understandable. But, in fact, my question -- well, let me explain more clearly. I think it is fair to say that perhaps you were not explained everything in detail with regard to all that was going on in your neighbourhood, for example, the soldiers that you mentioned earlier. Perhaps you were not told extensively what they did at the time, and you did not take part in what they did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Of course I was too young to be involved in any form of military activity. But we did know everything about what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And what was going on was that there were many soldiers in that area, the area where your building was located.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: The soldiers were a little bit downwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: You know, however, that the confrontation lines were quite nearby, the confrontation lines between the two warring parties.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Which specific point do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: I'm thinking about Nedzaric.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Here there was a confrontation line close to the building.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would request that another map be called up on the screen, another map that we have in our atlas, number -- 65 ter number 002829. May I ask the registrar to call that up because we don't have it in our documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The registrar will find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Can we rotate it and enlarge it a bit, if possible. Enlarge the section -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see in front of you Nedzarici on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: This is a map that was drawn up by the UNPROFOR that depicts the confrontation lines between the warring factions; the BiH army on the one hand and the Republika Srpska army on the other. Can you see this line -- these two lines surrounding Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: According to UNPROFOR, part of Nedzarici - in fact you lived in Nedzarici - but part of Nedzarici was within the control of the army of the Republika Srpska but completely surrounded by units of the BiH army. That is reflected by the yellow line. So my question is as follows: According to the UNPROFOR, there were military facilities around and within the yellow line, near the yellow line, because that line was the confrontation line. Would you agree with me in saying that the neighbourhood in which you lived was very near those two lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I wasn't living in Nedzarici, although maybe that's a lesser point. This is a rather bad map and I can only say approximately where my neighbourhood was, but I cannot say it with 100 per cent surety.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, well, with perhaps less certainty, exactly where was located your building? Approximately where was located your building?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we give the witness a pen so he can show us on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the building should approximately be in front of this yellow line here. Not completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the same building where the passage or the alleyway was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And does this map make it possible for you to indicate the location of the centre for blind children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It's very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: But am I correct in saying that it should be rather close by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes, it was close.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Earlier you mentioned the holes in that building, the centre for the blind. Do you remember mentioning that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see those holes yourself? And when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And when did you see them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: They were there throughout the whole war.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see them with your own eyes, or were these -- was this hearsay, things that you heard, that you heard the soldiers talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: I saw them with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us approximately where those apertures were in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Here?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, not at all. Since you are an eyewitness, I would ask you to describe them, because we've heard a great deal about this house. Perhaps you could describe this house, this building, and tell us where it was located at the time, and where those apertures were located that you saw with your own eyes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: The hole -- the wall where the holes were can clearly be seen in the video that was played with the reconstruction in which I took place. So when you look at this building there's a wall, and beneath the roof there were holes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'd like to see that again. Sorry, I'll take account of that in estimating your time. Can we see that video again so I can see those holes?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was also going to suggest that, but perhaps before that, since the witness has indicated his building, we could keep this as evidence, we could tender it as evidence, and have a number for this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps annotate it slightly with an X, for example. We see a straight line. Could you perhaps put an X or a star.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Are you referring to my building? [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be admitted as Exhibit D25, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can we then have the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, may I again request private session for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And when you said "dormitory," were you thinking of a place where the soldiers would sleep or where they would walk around, would come in and go out?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was a privately-owned flat where the soldiers were billeted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: And how did you know that, if it was a private apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It was common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Could it perhaps be because you saw the soldiers entering that apartment and exiting it? Is that perhaps why it was known?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: It was generally known. Not that I didn't see them. I did see a couple of them. But everybody knew that they were sleeping there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your statement, the second statement that you made on the 22nd of May, 2006, for the Prosecution - I don't know if it's really necessary to pull it up on the screen; perhaps if you remember it, we can just move ahead - you mention a person named Fahrudin, a friend of yours, and then soldiers. And in that statement -- perhaps it would be easier if it was called up on the screen, in order to refresh your memory, to make things easier for you. My assistant will call it up. Well, there are two versions, so we'll take a moment. The fourth page, paragraph 17. We also have it in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see it -- we don't see it on the screen. Does anyone see it on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you see paragraph 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: So for the interpreters, it is paragraph 17. I will read it in B/C/S. "When I was tending Adnan with Fahrudin at the department store, I recall some soldiers coming with a stretcher and putting bandages on Adnan. Adnan was trying to breathe but could not, and the soldiers tried to put a lot of bandages over his wounds to close them. I know these persons were soldiers because they were carrying rifles. They were all wearing uniforms."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There's a problem there. In the English, it says "They were not wearing uniforms." Can you just read the B/C/S and let it be translated, for that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the statement that I have, it is: "I know that these people were soldiers because they were carrying rifles. They were all wearing uniforms."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "I know these persons were soldiers --" correction. "There were a number of persons living in the area who I knew as soldiers, but they did not have uniforms."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The English translation is wrong, then. It says "They were not wearing uniforms."

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm sorry. I'd just like to point out that the procedure for taking statements is that the original is the English; then the English statement is translated into B/C/S. So if there was a translation problem, it was in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you see English fluently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: A little.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Did you make your statement in English?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Maybe we can clarify, because if you read on, further lines down in that paragraph, paragraph number 17, you can see that the English text reads that "there were a number of persons living in the area who I knew as soldiers, but they did not have uniforms." So the same suggestion is made twice in that paragraph, that the persons were not wearing uniforms. So maybe it is the B/C/S translation which is wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, is there a special uniform for the Territorial Defence? Because in the last sentence of paragraph 17, in English, it is said, [In English] "They were something like the Territorial Defence." [Interpretation] How would you explain that? What does that mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were no special uniforms. Each of these men would put on themselves whatever they had. Some had camouflage vests; some had trousers. I don't know. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, I will ask you again the question, regardless of what is written in the statement. It seems very odd to me that you would make a statement in English, since your language is B/C/S. But let me come back to the facts. At that time, those people who came to give you help, were they dressed as you just described to Judge Mindua?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS W-62
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, some were; some were not. Some were in civilian clothes; some of them only had a vest. I was in a state of shock and I didn't have either time or will to look closely at how everybody was dressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Isailovic, how much longer will you be? Because we are beyond the time when we should adjourn. We are now encroaching on the other Trial Chamber's trial time. Ms. Marcus, you'll be re-examining?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, very briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, in view of the fact that we are beyond the time when we should adjourn, I think we must break now. So we'll adjourn, and, regrettably, you'll have to return tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 24th day of January, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.49 p.m.,
